parsed.why: Second-highest risk tier; in-force facility law covering all schools and colleges by birth certificate, narrowing state ID rules, no state gender-identity protections, hostile legislative trajectory layered on the restrictive national document regime.

Hostile legislature, but courts repeatedly enjoin facility, care and ID restrictions under state constitution; only division improving in national tier. Rule of law working for trans people mitigates, though national passport/entry regime still binds.

Escalating tier: facility ban expanded to universities in 2026, birth-sex appropriations rules, one of four states with prison treatment-restriction policy, no hate-crime statute, unrepealed sodomy provision; adds custody exposure atop the national regime.

Low-risk tier with operating protections: statewide gender-identity discrimination ban with enforced remedies, X markers, city sanctuary order shielding travellers, no adult facility ban. No hate-crime statute and the hostile national document/entry regime cap the score.

Moderate tier but no adult facility or care restriction; youth measures and board rules mostly miss visitors. Weaknesses: no statewide non-discrimination coverage outside four cities, hate-crime gap, thin recourse, layered on the national document regime.
